summary: Just-in-time access shows approved but user lacks console roles after approval
summary_long: A developer used Just-In-Time (JIT) access to elevate for a support task; Okta approval flow completed, but the console still returns 403 and the user has no elevated roles in the UI or token claims.
description:
Issue summary: A developer requested temporary elevation via the internal JIT access flow. The approval email was clicked, approval registered in Okta (approval log entry present), but the user remains unable to access the support console and receives 403 errors when attempting role-protected routes.

Impact: Blocks a support engineer from accessing runbooks and incident dashboards for ~30 minutes. Internal impact only, affects a single on-call engineer.

Environment: Production (us-east), Console v2.34, Auth proxy v1.8, Okta org: redwood-prod.okta.com.

Observed at: 2026-03-10T14:22:00Z (first report).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) User initiates 'Request Temporary Elevation' from internal console.
2) Manager approves via Okta approval email.
3) User clicks approve and sees Okta confirmation.
4) User attempts to open /runbooks and /incidents in console and receives 403.
5) Token exchange logs show successful grant but console RBAC check fails.
expected_behavior: After Okta approval, the user's session and tokens should include the elevated role claims and the console should allow access to role-restricted pages within 30s.
actual_behavior: Okta logs show approval event and JIT service recorded a successful approval; however, the console shows '403 Forbidden' and the user's token does not include the temporary elevated roles. A manual re-login sometimes fixes the issue for affected users.
logs_and_evidence:
- Okta System Log entry: eventType=approval.task.approved id=0oab12345XYZ timestamp=2026-03-10T14:23:05Z
- JIT service log: approval_handler: processed approval id=apr-789, status=applied, assigned_role=oncall-temporary
- Auth proxy token-exchange log: token_exchange request id=te-456 status=200 claims=[base_roles] (missing oncall-temporary)
- Console audit: 403 on GET /runbooks for user maya.chen@redwood.com at 2026-03-10T14:24:21Z
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: race between approval propagation to RBAC cache and token exchange.
Findings: JIT service emitted 'status=applied' but role propagation worker showed spike of errors connecting to role-store (ETCD) between 14:23:30 and 14:24:10 (connection refused transient).
Second hypothesis: token issued before role write committed, so token lacks new claim. Evidence: token timestamp 14:23:40, role-store write commit at 14:24:05.
Added a temporary mitigation to refresh user session after approval to force re-fetch of claims.
temporary_workaround: Support instructs affected users to perform a full sign-out and sign-in after approval (or force token refresh). This restores access in >90% of cases. For the on-call engineer in this ticket this resolved the issue at 14:32 after sign-out.
root_cause: Propagation lag between JIT approval commit and RBAC store leading to tokens minted before role write completion. Underlying cause appears to be transient ETCD connectivity errors on role-store write worker during a brief network hiccup.
resolution:
- Restarted role-store write-worker to clear transient connection failures (14:50 UTC).
- Added a short retry/wait in the approval handler: after write commit verification, approval handler now polls role-store up to 3s to ensure role visible before returning success to token exchange.
- Instrumented a metric for approval-to-claim latency and alert if >5s.
- Follow-up: SRE to investigate ETCD networking noise in us-east (ticket INT-100215 linked).
